FRETBOARD HERO / FRETBOARD NOTES

Know where the next note lives.

The Fretboard Map shows where notes repeat across the guitar neck. Start with one note, use the open strings as landmarks and connect positions through octaves.

Try this exercise ↗Get it on Google Play

Written by Jean-François Seignemorte · Reviewed 27 October 2026

Use standard tuning as your starting point

From the lowest to the highest string, standard guitar tuning is E–A–D–G–B–E. Each fret raises the pitch by one semitone. At fret 12, you reach the same note name as the open string, one octave higher.

Learn one note across all six strings

Once A feels familiar, full access lets you select other notes or display the complete map. Move in small groups rather than trying to memorize every fret at once.

  1. Open the Fretboard Map and select A. This is the note available in the free demo.
  2. Find the nearest A on each string. Say its name and fret number before playing it.
  3. Look away from the map and repeat. Return to the diagram only when you need a check.

Connect the map to scales and chords

An A in the map can be the root of an A minor pentatonic pattern or an A minor triad. Open the corresponding guide and notice how the same note appears in different musical contexts.

The quiz adds timed recall practice for roots, thirds and fifths. It tests what you can identify on the displayed neck; use your guitar alongside it to connect the visual answer with a sound.

Questions before you start

Does the map follow alternate tunings?

These guitar exercises use the standard six-string tuning E–A–D–G–B–E.

Which notes are free?

The demo map focuses on A. Full access opens the other note filters and the complete note map.
